messages:
Rae: Sharing quick mock of the new Metrics strip view. Two questions: 1) how should we represent extreme outliers so the scale stays useful? 2) what should legend look like in compact panels? Screenshot attached.

Kai: For outliers I'd prefer a hard 'overflow' marker rather than hiding values silently. e.g. any point > 98th percentile gets an upward caret icon and counts as overflow. Clicking the caret expands the axis to show the real points.

Priya: +1 to making action explicit. UX microcopy suggestion: "Overflow values hidden to improve visibility. Show all values." The word 'hidden' might alarm users; maybe "compressed" instead?

Design-Lead: I'd avoid 'compressed' because it's unclear. Keep it simple: "Values above the 98th percentile are collapsed for readability. Show full range." Also prefer 98% as default for dashboards that surface lots of noise. We can make it configurable per panel.

Rae: Legend ideas: a compact layout that shows color swatch + short name + an overflow pill (e.g. "+5") when points are collapsed. Clicking series toggles visibility; keyboard needs to be supported.

Kai: Accessibility: include an offscreen status element that updates to "Series X collapsed to 98th percentile, 5 points hidden" whenever overflow state changes. Also each overflow caret should have aria-label like "expand to view overflow values".

Accessibility-Bot: Accessibility checklist updated: ensure overflow pill meets 4.5:1 contrast, focusable via keyboard, and exposed in live regions. Link: https://redwood.internal/accessibility/metrics-overflow.

Priya: Units: prefer short SI suffixes for axis ticks (ms, s). Suggest auto-scaling rule: show `ms` for values < 1000, `s` otherwise; always expose full unit in axis label (e.g. "Latency (ms)") to be explicit for screen reader users.

Kai: Smoothing presets: none, EMA-10m, rolling-mean-5m. Default OFF for any panel with precise thresholds. When smoothing is active show a small badge on the legend: "EMA 10m" with tooltip explaining the algorithm. Tooltip copy: "Exponential moving average (10m) applied to improve trend readability. Turn off for raw values."

Rae: Visual cue for overflow: a faint semi-opaque caret at the top of the plot area and a thin dashed line at the axis clamp boundary. The overflow pill in the legend should be clickable and toggle expansion. For exported PNG/SVGs we should expand by default to avoid losing data in reports.

Design-Lead: Color nits: current teal isn't great at small sizes. Propose swapping to #0b8043 for that series. Also ensure caret glyph has at least 4.5:1 contrast against panel bg.

Priya: Small code snippet for legend focus state and overflow pill styling:

```
.legend-item { display:flex; gap:6px; align-items:center }
.legend-item:focus { outline: 2px solid #0b8043 }
.overflow-pill { background:#f3f4f6; color:#111; padding:2px 6px; border-radius:999px; font-size:12px }
```

Kai: Regarding telemetry copy — when users hover the overflow pill, show exact counts and top hidden values like: "5 hidden values, top = 12.3s". Helps debugging.

Rae: I'll update the figma and add a small ARIA-only paragraph at the top of charts: "This chart collapses extreme values by default. Use legend or overflow caret to expand." Will ping for a11y review once pushed.

Accessibility-Bot: Marking this thread for a11y review cycle 11. Assigned: @Priya, @Kai.

Design-Lead: Thanks everyone. Can we land the compact legend + overflow behavior behind a feature-flag and test with a few dashboards next week?
